claim.why_it_matters: The optional-module half of the module/subset diagram is split into a separate table with no subset column, so the vertical extents that tie each optional module level to the High, Intermediate and Minimum subsets (RPW and ITR spanning all three, level 2 vs level 1 COM/DEB/SEG split inside Intermediate) are lost; the printed figure's subset relationship cannot be read from the markdown.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 833 (A-3) shows one figure: REQUIRED MODULES and OPTIONAL MODULES sit side by side over a shared COBOL SUBSETS axis (HIGH / INTERMEDIATE / MINIMUM). In the optional half, '1 RPW 0,1' and '1 ITR 0,1' are single cells that run the full height of all three subset rows. Communication, Debug and Segmentation each have one horizontal divider about halfway down the INTERMEDIATE row: '2 COM/DEB/SEG 0,2' sits above it and '1 COM/DEB/SEG 0,2' below it. The markdown has every cell value correct but puts the optional modules in a separate five-column table with no subset axis and plain stacked rows. That drops the row spans and the mid-INTERMEDIATE split. The claim quotes both sources accurately. The loss is structural, since the cell content survives and the header says 'Not Required in Subsets', but it is a real loss of figure information and not just formatting.
